podcast.body: This song was released by Living Colour in 1988, marking their emergence as a band that integrated metal, funk, punk, hip-hop, jazz, and alt-rock. The band was known for combining their fresh musical package with direct commentary on politics and race. "Four black eyes from New York City who brought together metal, funk, punk, hip-hop, jazz and alt-rock into one fresh package, mating it with straight commentary on politics and race."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song, released in 1988, was part of Living Colour's debut album "Vivid" and helped establish them as a significant band in the late 80s rock scene, contributing to their recognition as MTV heroes and Grammy winners. "Living color and cult of personality from 1988."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This track from their debut album "Vivid" won a Grammy for Best Hard Rock Performance and is one of their most recognized songs. "It won a Grammy for Best Hard Rock Performance, and is best remembered for this track. It's Cultiv personality."
